claims.text: Introducing an HPHT-treated Al0.7CoCrFeNi eutectic interlayer into HEA multilayers will shift the dominant creep mechanism from diffusion-mediated to dislocation-mediated creep.
Al0.7CoCrFeNi is an eutectic high-entropy alloy that can be subjected to HPHT treatment.
HPHT-treated Al0.7CoCrFeNi contains FCC and B2 phases.
HPHT-treated Al0.7CoCrFeNi forms a highly coherent FCC/B2 interface.
The FCC/B2 mismatch factor in the HPHT-treated alloy is near 0.004.
Standard or incoherent HEA multilayer interfaces predominantly exhibit diffusion-mediated creep at high temperature or low stress.
A thin HPHT-treated Al0.7CoCrFeNi layer can function as an interlayer in an HEA multilayer while retaining the proposed FCC/B2 interfacial structure.
A highly coherent FCC/B2 interface facilitates dislocation transmission across layers.
A highly coherent FCC/B2 interface impedes fast interfacial diffusion pathways.
Interface coherency reduces atomic diffusivity along the interface.
Interface coherency promotes the nucleation and glide of dislocations across multilayer interfaces.
Diffusion-mediated creep dominates at lower stresses or higher temperatures.
Suppressing interface diffusion while favoring dislocation activity causes the proposed creep-mechanism transition.
Multilayers containing the eutectic interlayer will have a lower creep rate in the dislocation-mediated regime than control multilayers lacking the interlayer.
The proposed mechanism will produce dislocation pile-ups and transmission across the coherent interface.
HEA multilayers without the engineered coherent interlayer are predominantly controlled by atomic diffusion along incoherent interfaces.
The transition effect is most pronounced where diffusion and dislocation creep are both competitive.
The transition effect diminishes at very high temperature when diffusion dominates and at very low temperature when diffusivity is negligible.
